response.original_title: What is PLC in real estate?
response.overview: PLC in real estate stands for Preferential Location Charges. It is an additional charge that a builder may apply when a property is located in a preferred or more desirable part of a residential project. For example, a flat with a park-facing, corner, road-facing, pool-facing, or higher-floor location may have PLC charges because these locations can offer better views, natural light, ventilation, privacy, or convenience. The PLC charges in real estate are usually calculated based on the size of the property and the applicable PLC rate. For example, if the PLC rate is ₹200 per sq. ft. and the property size is 1,000 sq. ft., the PLC would be ₹2,00,000. The actual PLC rate can differ from one project to another depending on the location and features of the property. In simple terms, PLC meaning in real estate is the extra amount paid for getting a preferred location within a project.
